messages:
sam-customer: Hey team — starting ~09:10 UTC we started seeing 429s from your hosted API in eu-west1. Clients are healthy, no code deploys. Most errors are at the top of the minute. example: 2025-03-14T09:10:00Z -> spike. Returning "rate limit exceeded" body. Not sure why RPM/TPM hit only at minute boundaries. Any quick checks?

lina-support: @sam-customer sorry about that — can you paste the raw response headers and one example request id? :eyes:

sam-customer: sure, here's one response: 

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: r-0a1b2c3d
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1678780200
Retry-After: 12

body: {"error":"rate limit exceeded","scope":"rpm"}

Also our client logs show a retry loop that fires on 429 with exponential backoff but with very small jitter, and a cron job that runs at :00 each minute which fans out ~250 small requests in parallel.

lina-support: thanks. two quick theories: 1) minute-aligned cron + client retries cause a request pileup at the boundary (thundering herd). 2) sliding-window vs fixed-window rate calculation mismatch — some internal routes use fixed 60s windows which can make top-of-minute spikes worse. we'll pull metrics.

aaron-sre: grabbing edge metrics from eu-west1 now. show me the ingestion spike shape. also did you rotate API keys recently? multiple keys aggregated can exceed account-level RPM.

sam-customer: no key rotation. only 3 keys, each from different hosts. spike is always at :00 and sometimes at :30. Attached a quick histogram: bursts near boundary.

ops-bot: Deploy webhook: roll/queue-handler v1.18 -> success @2025-03-14T08:59:42Z

maria-eng: Can you reproduce locally with a small script? Something like: 

```bash
for i in {1..250}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}' &
done; wait
```

That reproduces the top-of-minute pressure if you trigger at :00. Also check if you are using streaming sessions (they can create extra connection churn).

sam-customer: we are using short streaming sessions from mobile. but the cron is server -> non-streaming. the mobile ones are more continuous, not boundary aligned.

aaron-sre: From infra graphs: we see a 2.6x request-per-second blip that crosses the per-route RPM threshold for ~10s at minute boundary. The per-account bucket is a fixed-minute bucket on our rate limiter for legacy customers — that explains the sharp boundary behavior.

lina-support: ok, immediate mitigation options: 1) add jitter to your cron (0-30s random) 2) tune client retries to use full jitter and respect Retry-After 3) if you can, split cron into N smaller rounds across the minute. We can also enable a rolling window quota for you temporarily if you need a quick fix, but that requires ops assist.

sam-customer: can you enable the rolling window? we have a production SLA here.

maria-eng: @lina-support / @aaron-sre To enable rolling window or increase tolerances we need an ops ticket. If they want a short-term config we can do a per-customer soft-threshold bump for the next 24h. Need approval.

aaron-sre: filed INC-3721 for temporary rolling-window enable + rate bump, requested 24h window. also added a watch to alert if Retry-After > 10s for >5% requests.

ratebot: Alert: ratecap-eu-west1 account=sam-corp threshold=600rpm breached 2025-03-14T09:10:00Z -> duration 14s

sam-customer: thanks. we'll add jitter and patch the cron asap. can you confirm what counts toward RPM vs TPM? our tasks are small tokens but many requests.

lina-support: RPM counts request starts; TPM counts tokens produced. For streaming responses the initial request and each resumed chunk only count as tokens toward TPM, but if you re-open the stream repeatedly each open is a request. Short streaming sessions can increase RPM if you reopen often.

maria-eng: also check client concurrency. If you have N parallel workers each making M requests at boundary, total = N*M. Consider queueing or token bucket on client side.

sam-customer: implementing jitter now. quick question: is there a header to tell remaining RPM per-minute granularly so we can stop mid-cron?

lina-support: we expose X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset at response time. For more granular telemetry we can enable token-level traces in the console for a short window. I'll open a support ticket to enable that for you.

sam-customer: appreciate it. after applying jitter will monitor and update. thank you everyone :heart:

lina-support: np — follow-up checklist: 
- add 0-30s jitter to cron
- switch retry policy to full jitter and honor Retry-After
- consider splitting into 4 rounds across the minute
- ops: temporary rolling-window enable until 2025-03-15 09:00 UTC (INC-3721)

aaron-sre: monitoring link: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/sam-corp/alerts/INC-3721 — keeping an eye, ping here if you still see boundary spikes.

sam-customer: will do, closing loop later with post-patch metrics.
